target_customer: Property administrators and security companies running gated communities and buildings in Latin America
problem: Gated community access, visitor control and administration are manual and paper based.
product_category: Proptech access control and community management

founders.name: Marwa Hage
founders.background_notes: YC page: PropTech entrepreneur, TEDx organizer; Forbes calls her Marwa Alhaj.

founders.name: Carlos de la Guardia
previous_startups: Not named, YC page says second time entrepreneur

competitors.name: Neivor
competitors.what: Residential building management app in Colombia

competitors.name: Wihom
competitors.what: Residential complex management app in Colombia

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile and web app with QR access; facial recognition came later.

defensibility.rationale: Once installed in a building, switching has some cost, but several local rivals exist.

market_need_then: Forbes Colombia Dec 2021: targeting 2000 communities by Q1 2022; no spend data.

identity.mascot_or_character: Mario, a character who narrates the site

brand_strength.rationale: Site mascot and tone are distinctive but no outside brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: Munily is active, claims 950 plus properties and 190K residents across several countries, and has about 30 staff. Funding is small and sources conflict, which fits a capital efficient regional business. Traction numbers are company claims only.
notes: Seedtable lists $665K seed Feb 2022 and other aggregators give $970K to $1.45M totals; unverified. Traction (950 properties, 190K residents) is from the company site, undated. Education and prior employers not found. Forbes Colombia names Carlos de la Guardia, Khaled Alhaj, Marwa and Mitchell Contreras as founders. Competitor sources are 2021-12, within the batch.
